items.title: Lew Soloff interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, April 16, 2000
items.q: I listened to Roy Eldridge and Louis Armstrong when I was a little kid.

ctx.x: Yeah my conscious reason for picking up the trumpet was because it was shiny and the odd thing is that I — I don’t know how you would put it — but I wound up liking a dull, straight brass-looking horn. As my horn got dull and brass I liked it. Now I also have a beautiful, shiny gold trumpet that I like. I have two trumpets, both of them Bach trumpets, one an old one made in New York City in 1947. I got it second-hand about I’d say close to 20 years ago I got it. And it’s a magnificent instrument, but it doesn’t…
Yeah. And all those years later, like all of a sudden that came out. That’s really great.
